conventions.coordinate_precision: ~100 m; suitable for station assignment, not navigation

_schema.slug: Stable primary key. Never change after first write; data accumulates against it.
_schema.name: Display name. Safe to change.
_schema.wave.primary: Buoy actually queried today. NDBC WMO id, or null for non-wave sites.
_schema.wave.fallback: Used when primary is not delivering. May be geographically distant; UI must disclose substitution.
_schema.wave.intended_primary: Buoy that SHOULD serve this spot but is currently dead. Reassign here when the REVIVED tripwire fires.
_schema.county_station: State/county beach water quality monitoring station code (e.g. OC-080) from the data.ca.gov Beach Water Quality Monitoring Stations resource. Resolved by nearest-neighbour against Active, located stations only, and ONLY for spots tagged swim, surf, dive or tidepool. null means unresolved OR out of join scope -- read county_station_null_reason to tell which. Must never render as a pass.
_schema.county_station_distance_m: Great-circle metres from the spot to its matched station; null when there is no match. Replaces the 1.0.0 field county_station_distance_km.
_schema.county_station_suspect: true when the match exceeds 1000 m, meaning the station may sit on a different beach cell carrying different water. The UI must disclose a suspect match rather than render it as a clean reading. null when there is no match.
_schema.county_station_null_reason: Present only when county_station is null, and required whenever it is. States why the field is empty: out of join scope, or genuinely unresolved. A null county_station without this key is a bug.
_schema.audiences: Which audience filters include this spot. Drives column visibility, not thresholds.
_schema.tidepool_floor_ft: Tide height below which the reef is WORKABLE -- the level at which enough of the intertidal is out of the water to be worth the trip. NOT the level at which it is at its best; that is lower, and encoding it here silently rejects every ordinary usable day. UNCALIBRATED estimates; see tidepool_floor_confidence.
_schema.tidepool_floor_confidence: low = author estimate, needs local verification. verified = confirmed by someone who goes there.
_schema.floor_evidence: Append-only ledger of every method that has been run against this spot's floor, oldest entry first. Present on the 8 spots that carry a floor. It does NOT set tidepool_floor_ft -- that field is the value in force, a human sets it against this ledger, and the newest entry is not automatically the answer. Promotion of tidepool_floor_confidence to 'verified' takes two entries from DIFFERENT methods agreeing within 0.3 ft, at least one of them instrumented (lidar hypsometry, pressure logger, MARINe transect topography); two author_estimate or two inat_revealed entries are one method run twice. See calibration/floor-calibration.md section 7.
_schema.floor_evidence[].method: Which method produced the entry: author_estimate | lidar_hypsometry | inat_revealed | pressure_logger | marine_topography | published_threshold. Not free text; that list is the whole set.
_schema.floor_evidence[].source: The artifact the entry came from, named precisely enough to find again: dataset and product name, or the committed file and its version.
_schema.floor_evidence[].source_date: When the underlying data was acquired, not when it was downloaded. For an author estimate, the date that estimate was written.
_schema.floor_evidence[].value_ft: The floor this method produced, in ft above MLLW per conventions.datum. null means the run yielded no usable value -- read note to tell 'has not run' from 'ran and produced nothing usable'. A null value_ft with an empty note is a bug, on the same terms as county_station_null_reason.
_schema.floor_evidence[].datum_transform: The vertical datum transformation applied, with its version pinned, e.g. 'VDatum 4.7, NAVD88 -> MLLW'. null where none was applied because the source is already MLLW ft.
_schema.floor_evidence[].n: Sample count in whatever unit the method counts in; the note states the unit. null where the method has no sample count.
_schema.floor_evidence[].run_date: When this entry's value was computed or set.
_schema.floor_evidence[].note: What the run established, in prose. Required whenever value_ft is null. Figures that came from a generated file are summarised here, never copied, because a re-run rewrites them.
_schema.mpa: Marine protected area NAME from CDFW ds582, resolved by point-in-polygon. null means the point fell outside every MPA polygon. Do not hand-populate. Read together with mpa_resolved: a null with mpa_resolved false is unknown, not unprotected.
_schema.mpa_resolved: true once the CDFW point-in-polygon join has run AND the result survives this file's ~100 m coordinate precision. false where the spot lies within 150 m of an MPA boundary, i.e. inside the coordinate error bar, so the in/out call is not trustworthy either way. Legally load-bearing for the tidepool audience.

floor_evidence.source: spots.json 1.1.1 author estimate, raised +1.5 ft uniformly in 1.2.0

floor_evidence.source: MARINe site list, California South region (marine.ucsc.edu/sites/sites-region/sites-region-ca-south/) and the Swami's Beach site page, read for network membership and survey type; nearest Biodiversity Survey site coordinate from OBIS dataset bb638343-bbc9-464d-88d8-18d9ba29ecdd 'MARINe/PISCO: Intertidal: MARINe Coastal Biodiversity Surveys: Point Contact Surveys Summarized' (doi:10.6085/AA/marine_cbs.5.7), WGS84
floor_evidence.note: Ran and found no Biodiversity Survey site here, so no surveyed elevation exists at this spot at any distance. A MARINe site named 'Swami's Beach' does exist, but it runs Long-Term Monitoring only, established 2017 by National Park Service staff, and LTM has no topography component -- elevation along transects belongs to the Biodiversity Survey, which has never been run there. Its coordinate cannot be checked against ours either: MARINe's public LTM extracts hold no record south of 33.2 degrees N, so the San Diego LTM sites are absent from the machine-readable feed entirely. Name-matching would have misled twice over, because MARINe places its Swami's Beach site 'within Cardiff State Beach and the Swami's State Marine Conservation Area', which is south of Swami's proper. Nearest Biodiversity Survey site of any kind is MARINe's 'Cardiff Reef' at 32.99984, -117.27867, 4132 m away and a different reef by any reading. The instrumented route here remains lidar hypsometry.

floor_evidence.source: shared/calibration.json 1.1.0 (taxa 1.0.0, spots 1.3.1, content_hash 6ece7b19), read against the permissiveness rule in calibration/floor-calibration.md section 7: iNaturalist research-grade sightings of the frozen target taxa within 500 m, corpus from 2016-01-01, binned by the day's lowest predicted low at CO-OPS 9410230 (2016-2026, MLLW)
floor_evidence.note: A CEILING, not an estimate: the most permissive floor the rule allows on a band the gates may read, and it says nothing about where this reef actually surfaces. NOT A PROMOTION INPUT -- never one side of a section 7 clause-1 agreement comparison at any tolerance, because an upper bound from citizen-science inference and an instrumented measurement are not two estimates of one quantity. tidepool_floor_confidence stays low. Derivation, and the reason this value is the CONSERVATIVE end of a bracket: 2x this spot's background band is the bar, and walking up, the highest band clearing it is 0.00-0.25 ft -- but that band holds only 8 visits against the 15 a bin needs to be usable, so a ceiling of 0.25 ft would rest on a band no gate may read. The highest clearing band that IS usable is -0.50-0.00 ft, holding 51 visits. The true ceiling therefore lies somewhere in 0.00-0.25 ft and this corpus cannot say where; 0.00 ft is the end of that bracket that fails toward the restriction, which is the direction the rule requires. Worth flagging for whoever reads this next: this spot's background band is the widest of the three that publish, spanning 0.25-3.00 ft pooled from 6 bins, and its measured background moved by roughly half on a bin-width change alone between calibration.json 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 -- so the quantity being doubled here is the least stable of the three. n is 237 collapsed visits from 185 observers. Figures summarised rather than copied because a re-run rewrites them. The standing limitation: sighting rate is not walkability, so the curve's SHAPE is trustworthy at 9.67x amplitude and its LEVEL is an assumption.

spots.notes: Reef point. MPA UNRESOLVED: point-in-polygon puts this 18 m OUTSIDE Swami's SMCA, far inside this file's ~100 m coordinate precision, so neither in nor out can be asserted. Do not present collection rules from the mpa field until the coordinate is surveyed.

floor_evidence.note: UNRESOLVED in both directions, and deliberately not decided here. The Biodiversity Survey site 'La Jolla Caves', surveyed in 2009, 2013 and 2020, may or may not be this reef, because MARINe's own two accounts of where it is do not agree. Its published coordinate is 32.84323, -117.28120, which is 1142 m south of this spot on a west-facing stretch -- 3.1x the combined uncertainty of this file's ~100 m coordinates and the 350 m coordinateUncertaintyInMeters the MARINe dataset carries per record -- so on the coordinate alone it is a different reef. But MARINe's prose puts the site 'within the Matlahuayl State Marine Reserve' and describes it as north-facing on relatively flat terrain, which describes the Cove and Goldfish Point, essentially on top of this coordinate; and the ds582 join puts this spot 21 m from the Matlahuayl boundary, so the prose reading is entirely consistent with this being the site. One of the two is wrong and nothing public arbitrates: this spot's own mpa is null with mpa_resolved false, so the file cannot check the reserve claim either. Recorded as a conflict rather than as a distance, because picking either reading would either claim a reef that is not ours or discard one that is. Resolving it needs the survey's benchmark-bolt coordinate, which is not published. Highest-value follow-up of the eight, since this spot also refuses the revealed-preference method and is otherwise unreached.

Surveyed four times: 2012, 2018, 2020 and 2025. A surveyed elevation therefore exists, and Biodiversity Survey topography is an instrumented method under the section 7 promotion rule, which makes this the most valuable hit of the sweep: this spot refuses the revealed-preference method, so nothing else in this repo reaches it. value_ft is null because the number is not obtainable, NOT because it does not exist. No public MARINe product carries an elevation -- the point contact, quadrat and swath extracts all carry coordinates, event dates and depth 0.0, and no elevation or vertical-datum field of any kind -- topography is not among the assets the data-request page offers, and the datum is stated inconsistently: the survey-methods page says elevation is recorded relative to MLLW, while the Data Assets PDF of 2025-10-21 describes it as referenced to a per-site benchmark bolt and names no vertical datum anywhere in the document. A direct request to the survey PI is required, it must name the vertical datum explicitly or the answer is unusable, and none has been made. NOT A PROMOTION INPUT -- never one side of a section 7 clause-1 agreement comparison at any tolerance, because an upper bound from citizen-science inference and an instrumented measurement are not two estimates of one quantity. tidepool_floor_confidence stays low. Derivation, and the reason this value is the CONSERVATIVE end of a bracket: 2x this spot's background band is the bar, and walking up, the highest band clearing it is 0.25-0.50 ft -- but that band holds only 14 visits, one short of the 15 a bin needs to be usable, so a ceiling of 0.50 ft would rest on a band no gate may read. The highest clearing band that IS usable is 0.00-0.25 ft, holding 31 visits. The true ceiling therefore lies somewhere in 0.25-0.50 ft and this corpus cannot say where; 0.25 ft is the end of that bracket that fails toward the restriction, which is the direction the rule requires. One more visit in the 0.25-0.50 band would resolve it. n is 404 collapsed visits from 264 observers. Figures summarised rather than copied because a re-run rewrites them. The standing limitation: sighting rate is not walkability -- the curve's SHAPE is trustworthy at 5.93x amplitude, its LEVEL is an assumption -- and this spot's own notes say a wrong floor here strands people, which is a further reason to take the strict end.

tidepool_floor_ft values are UNVERIFIED at confidence 'low' on all 8 spots. As of 1.4.0 three of them (swamis, sunset-cliffs, cabrillo-tidepools) are no longer author estimates but CEILINGS derived from observed sighting rates -- upper bounds on how permissive the floor may be, not measurements of where the reef surfaces. The other 5 remain the 1.2.0 author estimates. Sunset Cliffs and Cabrillo are still the two that most need local verification.

1.2.0 raised all 8 tidepool_floor_ft by exactly 1.5 ft. The 1.1.x values (-0.8 to -0.2) encoded EXCELLENT tidepooling, not workable tidepooling, and the difference is not cosmetic: over the 7 days from 2026-07-28, station 9410230 put 49 of the 56 grid cells in 'above-floor' -- the reef never surfaces -- and the remaining 7 in 'dark'. Not one usable window in a week, which is not what a week of San Diego tides looks like. Two independent sources put the workable threshold at about +1 ft MLLW and reserve negative tides for 'best' (tidepooling.org/learn: 'The best tidepooling happens during very low tides, typically below 1 foot'; lajollamom.com/best-san-diego-tide-pools: 'Low tide is less than 1 foot ... if you see a tide chart say -1 or lower, that's the best time to go'). The shift is a single constant applied uniformly rather than eight fresh guesses, so the author's RELATIVE ranking of the eight reefs is preserved intact and one number reverses the whole change. Band is now +0.7 to +1.3, straddling the +1 ft figure both sources give. Still confidence 'low'; still not field-checked.

SAFETY, stated in the direction that matters. The 1.2.0 shift moved every floor in the PERMISSIVE direction -- a higher floor means the stack calls a window open at higher water than it used to. 1.4.0 moved three of them back the other way: swamis +0.9 to 0.0, sunset-cliffs +0.7 to +0.25, cabrillo-tidepools +1.3 to +1.0. All three are STRICTER than what they replace, which is the direction a ceiling derived from a permissiveness rule can move in. sunset-cliffs went -0.8 to +0.7 in 1.2.0 and its own notes say a wrong floor there strands people; it is now +0.25, and it is no longer the strictest of the eight because swamis is at 0.0. Strictest-of-eight was always a ranking rather than a verification, and it still is: nobody has stood on that ledge system at any of these values and confirmed it. The 5 unchanged floors remain 1.2.0 author estimates in the permissive direction. Field-check Sunset Cliffs and Cabrillo before any of these numbers is presented as advice.
Per-spot surf threshold offsets are not yet modelled. Black's and Tourmaline are the clearest cases where a shared buoy reading means very different things.

floor_evidence is populated on all 8 tidepool spots and records that not one floor has instrumented evidence behind it. Every spot's first entry is method 'author_estimate', carrying the 1.1.1 value and the uniform +1.5 ft raise 1.2.0 applied to all 8. All 8 stay tidepool_floor_confidence 'low': the promotion rule needs two different methods agreeing within 0.3 ft with at least one instrumented, nothing in this repo is instrumented, and the inat_revealed entries are upper bounds that are explicitly barred from being one side of that comparison. As of 1.4.0 every spot carries an inat_revealed entry against shared/calibration.json 1.1.0. On the 3 that publish (swamis, sunset-cliffs, cabrillo-tidepools) it carries a value_ft and that value is now the floor in force -- a CEILING from the permissiveness rule, not an estimate. On the 5 that refuse (cardiff-reef, torrey-pines-beach, la-jolla-shores, la-jolla-cove, windansea) value_ft is null and the note says what refused, so 'no evidence gathered' can be told apart from 'evidence gathered and it refused'; none of those 5 floors moved. The earlier entries against calibration.json 1.0.0 are kept unedited because this ledger is append-only, and their per-bin counts and amplitude ratios are superseded: 1.0.0 used 6 bins and read background off a single bin, 1.1.0 uses 10 and pools the background band.

The MARINe Biodiversity Surveys site list has been checked against all 8 tidepool spots as of 1.3.1, and every spot now carries a marine_topography entry -- but not one of them carries an elevation, so the sweep changed no floor and promoted nothing. What it found: 3 spots sit on a Biodiversity Survey site (cabrillo-tidepools 70 m from 'Cabrillo I', windansea 236 m from 'Wind and Sea', sunset-cliffs 437 m from 'Sunset Cliffs'); 1 is unresolved (la-jolla-cove, where the published coordinate for 'La Jolla Caves' is 1142 m away but MARINe's prose places that site inside Matlahuayl SMR, essentially on top of this spot, and nothing public arbitrates); and 4 are not in the network at all (swamis, cardiff-reef, torrey-pines-beach, la-jolla-shores). Distances are read against a combined 1-sigma of 364 m -- this file's ~100 m coordinates and the 350 m coordinateUncertaintyInMeters the MARINe dataset carries per record -- so 70 m and 236 m are not distinguishable from zero, 437 m is the awkward middle and is deliberately NOT called same-bench, and anything past 1 km is a different reef. Two spots would have been bound to the wrong reef by name alone: MARINe's 'Cardiff Reef' is 1950 m from ours, at the south end of Cardiff State Beach by MARINe's own description, and MARINe's 'Swami's Beach' runs Long-Term Monitoring only, which has no topography component. The elevation itself is NOT PUBLISHED anywhere: the three Coastal Biodiversity Survey extracts carry coordinates, event dates and depth 0.0 and no elevation or vertical-datum field, topography is not among the assets MARINe's data-request page offers, and the datum is stated inconsistently between the survey-methods page (elevation relative to MLLW) and the Data Assets PDF of 2025-10-21 (referenced to a per-site benchmark bolt, no vertical datum named anywhere in the document). So MARINe does not remove the lidar deliverable anywhere. At 3 spots it converts that work from modelling an elevation to requesting one and pinning its datum, and THAT REQUEST HAS NOT BEEN MADE; for la-jolla-shores, cardiff-reef and torrey-pines-beach lidar remains the only instrumented route. n is null on all 8 entries because a site-list lookup has no sample count: the survey-round counts are stated in each note rather than borrowed into a field that means collapsed visits on the inat_revealed entries. All 8 stay tidepool_floor_confidence 'low'. Section 7 does list MARINe transect topography as an instrumented method, so this sweep looks like it unlocks promotion, and it does not: with value_ft null there is nothing for a second method to agree with.

1.4.0 set three tidepool_floor_ft values from the permissiveness rule declared in calibration/floor-calibration.md section 7: no floor may admit a marginal band whose observed sighting rate is below 2x that spot's own tide-independent background. swamis +0.9 to 0.0, sunset-cliffs +0.7 to +0.25, cabrillo-tidepools +1.3 to +1.0. What these values ARE: ceilings -- the most permissive floor the rule allows on a band holding at least the 15 visits a bin needs to be usable. What they are NOT: measurements of the elevation at which each bench surfaces. Nobody has surveyed any of them and the rule is silent about where the floor actually is; it only forbids values above these. Only cabrillo-tidepools has a crossing this corpus can locate exactly, on a marginal band of 30 visits. sunset-cliffs and swamis are the CONSERVATIVE END OF A BRACKET: at both, the band that would justify a higher ceiling clears the rate bar but holds fewer than 15 visits -- 14 at sunset-cliffs, one short, and 8 at swamis -- so the true ceiling lies somewhere above the value set and this corpus cannot say where. Both were resolved downward because the rule fails toward the restriction. The remaining limitation does not go away with more data of this kind: SIGHTING RATE IS NOT WALKABILITY. The gate asks whether the bench is workable; the curve measures whether somebody photographed a target species. The relationship is monotone across every usable bin at all three spots, so the SHAPE is trustworthy -- the LEVEL is an assumption, and it is the reason confidence stays 'low' and the reason the lidar deliverable is not optional. The other 5 floors are untouched; those spots refuse the method and no amount of additional citizen-science data sets a floor there.
